question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [European Colonial Administrative Headquarters]
options: Pondicherry — French administrative capital in India
Goa — Portuguese administrative capital of Estado da India
Calcutta — Capital of British Presidency of Fort William
Chinsurah — Danish East India Company's administrative headquarters in Bengal
wrong_fact: Chinsurah was not the Danish East India Company's administrative headquarters in Bengal; it was the headquarters of the Dutch East India Company (VOC) in Bengal. The Danish administrative headquarters in Bengal was Serampore.
explanation: The French established Pondicherry as their administrative capital. Goa served as the capital of Portuguese Estado da India from 1510. Calcutta was the capital of Fort William presidency. Chinsurah was a Dutch settlement from 1656, while Serampore (Fredericknagore) was the Danish headquarters in Bengal.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Charter Cities and Municipal/Legal Institutions]
options: Madras — First Municipal Corporation established by British in India (1688)
Bombay — Portuguese administrative center ceded as dowry to the British Crown (1661)
Pondicherry — Site of the French Conseil Supérieur (Supreme Council) established in 1701
Surat — First Mayor's Court established under the Charter of 1726
wrong_fact: The first Mayor's Courts under the Royal Charter of 1726 were established in Madras, Bombay, and Calcutta, not in Surat.
explanation: The Charter of 1726 authorized the East India Company to establish Mayor's Courts in the three presidency towns of Madras, Bombay, and Calcutta, introducing English judicial procedures. Madras Municipal Corporation was created earlier in 1688. Bombay was indeed ceded to Britain by Portugal in 1661. The Conseil Supérieur was the apex French administrative and judicial body in Pondicherry.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Administrative Enclaves and Revenue/Customs Jurisdictions]
options: Tranquebar (Tharangambadi) — Danish administrative enclave paying tribute to the Tanjore Kingdom
Yanam — French enclave on the Andhra coast under Pondicherry administrative control
Masulipatnam — Dutch factory regulated by the Golconda Sultanate's golden firman
Chandernagore — Portuguese administrative enclave annexed to the Madras Presidency
wrong_fact: Chandernagore was a French administrative enclave in Bengal (not Portuguese) and was never part of the Madras Presidency.
explanation: Chandernagore was established by the French in 1673 and remained a French territory until it was merged with India in 1950. Tranquebar was the Danish headquarters in South India, paying tribute to the Tanjore Rajas. Yanam was a French outpost on the Godavari delta. Masulipatnam's Dutch factory operated under royal firmans of the Golconda kings.
